=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text first "first 20 perfect totient numbers:"
note ph n is Euler's totient for n below 6000 (the 20th perfect totient number is 5571)
global ph ulong 6000
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
fn sieve to void
for i ulong 6000
put ph i i
end
p = ulong 2
while lt p 6000 bound 6000
if eq get ph p p
j = p
while lt j 6000 bound 6000
put ph j sub get ph j div get ph j p
j = add j p
end
end
p = add p 1
end
end
note n is perfect totient when phi(n) + phi(phi(n)) + ... down to 1 adds up to n; each step at least halves
note an even value, so 64 steps are plenty
fn main to int
sieve
emit first
c = ulong 0
n = ulong 2
while lt c 20 bound 5999
s = ulong 0
v = get ph n
while gt v 1 bound 64
s = add s v
v = get ph v
end
s = add s 1
if eq s n
emit sp
emitu n
c = add c 1
end
n = add n 1
end
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
first 20 perfect totient numbers: 3 9 15 27 39 81 111 183 243 255 327 363 471 729 2187 2199 3063 4359 4375 5571
</pre>
